# Sleepy · 轻课表

> Factual index for AI retrieval, following https://llmstxt.org/. Android product baseline: v1.0.63, published 2026-11-01T17:06:44Z. Reviewed 2026-11-02 against https://github.com/lingion/sleepy/tree/v1.0.63 (commit b16aa84d11c250acdf644cd8b7812ab27d03dc6a). Later main commits and debug builds are not shipped v1.0.63 features. Release availability follows the versioned release page.

- Wiki: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy/wiki ; issues: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy/issues
- Native iOS project: https://github.com/lingion/sleepy-ios . Its own documentation and Releases govern installation and availability; do not infer full Android parity or an installation method from this Android baseline.
- Current separate iOS public-beta entry: https://testflight.apple.com/join/SxymmDzf. The iOS project defines its own release scope; this is not a claim of Android feature parity.
- Interactive web trial: https://sleepy.is-my.app/preview . It is not a full-feature equivalent of either native app. No native Windows edition is offered.
- Android minimum API 26 (Android 8.0), target and compile SDK 37. versionName 1.0.63, versionCode 10063.
- Release package: com.lingion.sleepy. Debug package in this source: com.lingion.sleepy.debug, with separate data.
- Four release APKs: arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a (V7A), x86_64, universal. Verify downloads against the release sha256sums.txt.
- UI languages: Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese and Spanish. The website has Chinese and English surfaces.

## Account, storage, privacy and network boundaries

No Sleepy account, email, phone number, subscription or paid tier is required. Manual entry and saved timetable viewing/editing work offline. Academic import may require a school account, student number, password or captcha entered in the school's WebView. This is separate from registering with Sleepy.

Timetables and preferences are stored locally. The source does not integrate Firebase Analytics, Crashlytics, Sentry, Bugsnag, AppCenter or Bugly analytics/crash-reporting SDKs. Academic passwords are not written to the timetable database; school WebView sessions or cookies are a separate matter. Do not claim that local storage means every operation avoids servers.

Network operations include school academic import, WakeUP online share-token resolution through the third-party api.wakeup.fun service, public holiday-data refresh, GitHub/mirror update checks and downloads. System calendar export, file sharing and backups intentionally transfer data to the chosen destination. Never publish credentials, cookies, tokens, captchas or identifiable schedules in issues or test fixtures.

## Timetables and editing

- Multiple local course tables with independent start dates, maximum weeks and period schedules.
- Time-grid and grouped week views, plus a Today page. Wide landscape layouts can use two panes; portrait tablets fall back to one pane.
- Overlapping courses remain in data; conflict layouts expose stacked entries rather than deleting obscured courses.
- Single occurrence adjustment changes one dated session instead of the parent recurring course rule. Recurring edits remain separate.
- Long-press course dragging uses grid landing positions. Edge dwell triggers continuous week paging every 500 ms within week boundaries. An empty cell opens a quick-add capsule with day/period prefilled. Do not attribute later main drag-scroll or release-gesture fixes to this release.
- Undo/redo uses an in-process history, default 5 steps. Laboratory settings support configurable depth: 0 disables history, a negative depth removes the step limit. New edits clear redo; process termination loses history. This is not a backup or a universal rollback for external/calendar/diagnostic writes.
- Period schedules support manual per-period start/end editing and automatic calculation from first time, duration, count and break templates. Different course tables can bind different period tables.
- Period header timestamp alignment is configurable. Week views can show calendar dates; long gaps use floating strips instead of excessive empty row height.
- A ghost indicator preserves the original slider value or bounds for comparison while editing; it is not a second active course or range.

## Academic catalog and release status

The v1.0.63 app/src/main/assets/schools.json snapshot contains 4140 unique catalog entries. Status normalization follows JwSchoolInfo:

- Configured baseline: 352, comprising supported 350 and grad_supported 2. Of these, 348 omit status and normalize to supported; they are not an additional subtotal.
- Unverified: 2528, comprising unverified 2480 and grad_unverified 48.
- Pending: 1260, comprising pending 1007 and grad_pending 253; these cannot directly start academic imports.

This is not a live-verified school count or a guarantee of successful import. A usable URL, registered parser, school availability and sometimes explicit confirmation are still required. Sources and boundaries are recorded in docs/catalog/manifest.json and docs/catalog/README.md.

The Shiguang lineage covers 264 source institutions; only 43 final records select sg_asset. Do not convert source coverage into claims of 264 tested sg_asset adapters. Protocol families include Wisedu, Qiangzhi variants, Zhengfang variants, URP variants, classic_eams, eams5, Kingo, Chaoxing and school-specific adapters. Registration-only routes are not equivalent to tested parsers.

Jiamusi's supported configuration and Kingo parser corrections belong to v1.0.63; this is not evidence that every Kingo school was live-tested. School requests should use the public school_adaptation.yml issue template with public URLs and sanitized reproduction evidence. Successful unverified imports can produce a manually copied report; this reporting action does not automatically upload it.

## Input, sharing and export

Supported offline inputs: WakeUp share text beginning with 【来自WakeUp课程表】, WakeUp JSON, iCalendar/ICS, CSV, HTML tables, tab-separated text and native sleepy-v1 text with a chk integrity field. Content detection does not require selecting an internal parser name.

Online WakeUP share tokens are a separate input path. Resolution makes two POST requests to api.wakeup.fun, using /pluto/app/antispam and /share_schedule/getv2. It requires internet and a valid token and depends on the third-party service; expiration or protocol changes can fail independently of offline import.

Exports include WakeUp-compatible JSON, ICS and native sleepy-v1. The visible text-sharing entries use native sleepy-v1, not WakeUp's URL-encoded sharing format. Period tables have a narrower JSON/native export set. Android 10+ uses Download/Sleepy for applicable files; Android 8–9 uses app cache/FileProvider, while text sharing uses the Android share sheet.

The export page also offers a Xiaomi/XiaoAi importer deep link; final acceptance depends on the receiving client. ICS can be consumed by calendar apps.

## Backup, calendar and optional permissions

General Settings data migration exports .sleepybackup with timetable/database data, preferences and widget configuration. Merge appends tables while matching preference keys take backup values. Overwrite replaces included modules, preserving preference files absent from the backup. A single timetable JSON/ICS is not a full backup.

Calendar export previews a writable device calendar/date range before confirmation and requests calendar permissions for that action. A hidden local calendar can be created when needed; fingerprint-based incremental writes avoid ordinary duplicate exports, but this is not two-way real-time synchronization. First-period calendar alarms remain experimental and client-dependent.

Common optional permissions/settings include location after school Locate, notifications when enabling reminders, calendar access, exact alarms, battery optimization exemption, DND access and unknown-source update installation. Background services and boot restoration have system constraints. This is not an exhaustive Manifest permission inventory; offline viewing does not require granting all optional permissions.

## Widgets and reminders

Five widget families: Today, TwoDay, WeekList, WeekView and WeekGrid. The release contains 13 widget configuration XML files. Rendering uses synchronous RemoteViews + Canvas with theme/course colors shared with the app. The gallery uses the largest card as the row-height reference and centers scaled smaller previews. Refresh uses broadcasts, scheduled work and course boundaries; launcher/OEM restrictions can still interfere.

OriginOS desktop widgets use standard Android AppWidget, not a certified native atomic-widget offering. Vendor atomic-island/live cards are notification surfaces, not these home-screen widgets. Earlier Glance SessionWorker freezing on ColorOS explains the move to synchronous rendering, not a guarantee that every launcher is unrestricted.

Pre-class reminders accept 1–999 minutes; today/tomorrow summary times and date rules are configurable. In v1.0.63 summaries aggregate all timetables into one time-sorted notification, using timetable-name prefixes when needed. Later current-table-only changes are not in this baseline. Each timetable has reminder toggles.

Banner and experimental live-card modes are mutually exclusive. Switching to banner stops live-card delivery. Android 16 Live Updates has a device-specific RMX6688/ColorOS16 record; Pantanal/Seedling SDK and UPK paths must not be presented as fully integrated. Delivery-service status does not prove the OS displayed a capsule. See docs/vendors/oppo-coloros-fluid-cloud.md.

AlarmManager provides exact/inexact scheduling paths; BootReceiver restores scheduling after reboot/update. Optional class DND restores prior state after class. Notification permissions, device power management and OEM policy affect actual delivery. Closing reminder toggles stops new app scheduling; system notification settings remain separate.

## Appearance and graphics

System-following/light/dark modes, preset and custom palettes. Android 12+ can use Material You app dynamic colors; custom primary/secondary/tertiary/surface inputs are supported. Saving the active custom theme reapplies it.

Course colors have three modes: classic golden-angle HSL, theme-following, and custom seed. Group hues are persisted and shared with widgets; the golden angle is not the only rule across all modes. Theme-card selection reserves a fixed indicator slot.

Material 3 Expressive transitions and liquid-glass navigation are present. RuntimeShader rendering involves Android 13/API 33 graphics APIs, distinct from the whole app's API26 minimum. v1.0.63 has known limitations on some older devices; do not claim identical rendering or complete fallback everywhere, or silently include later compatibility fixes. Android 13 themed launcher icons use a monochrome layer and depend on launcher support, separate from Android12 app colors.

## Local diagnostic console

An opt-in authenticated diagnostic console binds to 127.0.0.1:3737. Requests use X-Sleepy-Token. After unlocking, it supports reads and selected create/update/delete operations for tables, courses, period schedules and preferences; it is not read-only. Release endpoints impose additional restrictions on catalog overrides, trigger and mock operations.

Do not expose it to the Internet or give tokens to untrusted tools. Writes can affect real data; back up first. Resetting a diagnostic session does not guarantee reversal of arbitrary changes. Public technical contract: docs/agent-debug-console/AGENT-SKILL.md.

## Development and contribution

JDK17, Kotlin/Kotlin DSL, Jetpack Compose/Material3, Room, Kotlin serialization, KSP, jsoup, WorkManager and RemoteViews/Canvas are used. For this product baseline check out tag v1.0.63 before ./gradlew assembleDebug or ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest. Source tests are under app/src/test. Current CI instructions at docs/ci-automation.md may describe tooling added after the release and do not change the APK's shipped features.

Read public CONTRIBUTING.md for scoped contributions. Keep all captures and fixtures sanitized. Current main docs may receive editorial corrections without modifying the released binary.
